title: DGX Spark - Databases / Data Stores
description: PostgreSQL server statistics plus the DuckDB warehouse, both LanceDB indexes, Parquet and reports.

options.content:
This platform's data lives in **two very different places**, and both are on
this page.

**PostgreSQL** holds application state — conversations, messages, cross-chat
memory, the web-search memory (`web_pages`, `web_searches`, `web_results`),
crawl records and Deep Research runs. It has a real exporter, so everything
below is live server statistics.

**Files on the `data` volume** hold everything else, and none of them speak a
wire protocol: the Salesforce warehouse is a **DuckDB** file, the two vector
indexes are **LanceDB** directories, and the sync worker lands **Parquet**.
Those are measured by walking the volume read-only — size, file count, and how
long ago anything was written.

The number to watch is **warehouse snapshot age**. The sync worker publishes an
atomic read copy each cycle; if that age keeps climbing, every Salesforce
answer is quietly being served from a stale copy while every container still
reports healthy.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Against PostgreSQL's default max_connections of 100.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Below ~98% means the working set no longer fits in shared_buffers.

panels.title: Oldest client transaction
panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction of any client backend (0 when none). Replaces pg_long_running_transactions, whose 0.16.0 query counted background processes and reported the current time as its age.

panels.title: Rows per table
panels.description: Live-row estimates - conversations, messages, web memory, research runs.

panels.title: Dead tuples (vacuum pressure)
panels.description: Rising dead tuples with no autovacuum means bloat.

panels.title: Live throughput - what the database is doing right now
Read throughput
panels.description: PostgreSQL counts I/O in 8 KiB blocks; this converts to bytes/sec. Disk reads near zero means the whole working set is cached.

panels.title: Rows/sec
panels.description: 'returned' far above 'fetched' means sequential scans are reading rows the query then discards - the classic missing-index shape.

panels.title: Data store write rate
panels.description: How fast each file store is growing. Sampled every 30 s, so this is a 5-minute average rather than an instantaneous rate - a sync cycle or a crawl shows up as a step.

panels.title: Total data on disk
panels.description: Every measured store combined.

panels.title: Warehouse snapshot age
panels.description: How stale the Salesforce data is. The sync worker republishes this snapshot every cycle; a climbing age means answers come from an old copy while everything still looks healthy.

panels.title: Store growth
panels.description: LanceDB grows with every page the crawler stores; Parquet is never pruned.

panels.title: Time since last write
panels.description: A sawtooth is healthy - it resets each time the store is written. A line climbing forever means nothing is updating it.

panels.title: Stores present
panels.description: A fresh install has no warehouse until the first sync completes.

panels.title: Database timing (orchestrator side) and PostgreSQL internals
Statement p95 by call site
panels.description: One execute() round trip on the app-state pool, p95 over 5 m, per call site (app/db_metrics.py). Dashed line: the 5 ms hot-path target.

panels.title: Transaction p95 by call site
panels.description: Pool checkout to commit/rollback, p95 over 5 m, per call site: every statement, the Python between them and the COMMIT.

panels.title: Statements/sec by call site
panels.description: Round trips per second from this orchestrator. With no traffic this is the background polling rate (target: 1/s per process in total).

panels.title: Pool checkout and thread wait (p95)
panels.description: Checkout includes the pool's liveness check round trip. Thread wait is db.run_in_thread's queue for anyio's worker threads.

panels.title: Pool connections
panels.description: psycopg_pool counters sampled at scrape: connections held, idle, threads waiting for one, and the max_size ceiling (APP_DB_POOL_MAX).

panels.title: Checkpoints per hour
panels.description: pg_stat_checkpointer (monitoring/exporters/postgres/queries.yaml). Requested checkpoints are forced by WAL volume (max_wal_size) or a CHECKPOINT command; timed ones by checkpoint_timeout.

panels.title: WAL generated
panels.description: pg_stat_wal: bytes of WAL generated per second.

panels.title: WAL fsyncs by backend
panels.description: pg_stat_io (object = wal). client_backend fsyncs are commit flushes (synchronous_commit=on); walwriter is the background flush.

panels.title: Checkpoint write and sync time
panels.description: Milliseconds per second spent writing and fsyncing checkpoint buffers.

panels.title: Lock waits
panels.description: Sessions waiting on a heavyweight lock right now, and ungranted lock requests. pg_locks_count counts granted locks too, so it cannot show a wait.

panels.title: Transaction age
panels.description: Oldest open client transaction, and the longest current idle-in-transaction session.
